newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - April 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - April 24.

text.p: The following stories appeared in Thursday's Daily Variety:
* Foreign box office grosses from film "Ransom" and "101 Dalmatians" helped lift Walt Disney's overall profit 63 percent to $333 million in its second quarter.

* The movie "Rambo" could receive a new life if Miramax's genre division Dimension Films' floor bid of $500,000 for sequel and prequel theatrical film, TV and video rights is accepted by the federal bankruptcy court handling the liquidation of Carolco Pictures.
* For Tuesday night, Nielsen showed Disney's ABC averaged an 11.2 rating and 19 share, and won in total viewers and adults. General Electric's NBC finished second followed by Westinghouse's CBS.
* Academy Award-winning actor Cuba Gooding Jr is in final negotiations on a deal that would land him $1.5 million to star with Robin Williams in Interscope's "What Dreams May Come," sources said.
* The final piece of the Cannes Film Festival puzzle falls into place Thursday as the Directors Fortnight unveils a lineup containing a raft of debut films.

* Adding to the growing slate of projects based on his books, Elmore Leonard has struck a $1 million against $3 million deal with Universal Pictures for his upcoming historical novel Cuba Libre, which Brillstein-Grey Entertainment will produce.
